featured.name: Monad Auctions
featured.tagline: Continuous clearing auction for tokenized equities, settled with x402 upto on Monad
featured.desc: Monad hackathon build, 25 July 2026. x402's upto scheme is documented as metering — authorize a maximum, charge actual usage. Read as an auction it is already a bid: bidders sign a gasless, capped demand curve off-chain, every fill in a round clears at one uniform price, and losing bids cost nothing — no fee, no gas, no state. Price discovery for a tokenized stock stops being a guess someone has to make up front, and allocation stops going to the fastest bot: every bid above clearing fills pro-rata at it. Every price re-derives from the published bid set.

papers.title: The Funding Carry and a Cross-Venue Spread on Perpetual Futures: A Significance-Tested Study of Hyperliquid and Centralized Venues
papers.desc: Hyperliquid's hourly funding structurally exceeds Binance and Bybit on the same assets by roughly 7% annualized (14.7% in 2024, 4.6% in 2025). Held delta-neutral — long the centralized-venue perpetual, short the Hyperliquid one — the dislocation survives basis, capital and transaction costs at about 7–11% on deployed capital, and stays significant under Newey-West HAC t-stats of 4–8, a block bootstrap, five-fold walk-forward and a Deflated Sharpe. A battery of "smart" refinements — cost-recovery exits, cross-sectional allocation, ML tilts, options tail-hedging — all fail to beat the naive baseline; those nulls are reported as a catalog of holdout-selection artifacts.
